section.title: The Arena and the Apartment
section.form_description: A speech meant to move someone to act — the narrator talking Shepard (or whoever is listening) up off the floor and back into the fight. Sections are the rising beats of an address: the stakes named, the doubt named plainly, the evidence from a life lived that it can be done, the call. The narrator's own history is fuel for the exhortation, not the subject of it — but so is the listener's: the narrator holds up the other person's record as often as their own, since it's their record the speech is meant to land on.
section.form_note:
The brief is a speech, not a life story: Jack talking Shepard up in the last hour before the last push, using her own record as proof it can be done. Set after the Cerberus coup, the Citadel DLC shore leave, and the Cronos Station assault, this is the morning of the London conduit assault on Earth — everything is already staged (ships loaded, the plan set, the crew briefed), and the only thing left to do is get up and launch it. Jack is rousing Shepard right before he walks out to fight, not settling him in for the night. Romanced Jack per canon.choices (romance: Jack), consummated per jack_meeting/normandy-engineering scene at the end of ME2, with the Citadel DLC back tattoo. Note: choices.yaml's citadel_coup detail says Thane "died protecting the dalatrass," but the event record (thane-krios-death-defending-the-salarian-councilor) and the coup scene (citadel-coup-csec-office-kai-leng) both have him dying for the Salarian Councilor — treating this as the user's shorthand slip, not a real contradiction, and writing it as the Councilor. Per Thomas's request, "what-cerberus-made-me-for" and "the-kids-at-grissom" were rebuilt off shared Shepard/Jack history and broader lore instead of the Teltin and Grissom backstory events: recruitment off the Purgatory prison ship (jack-recruitment-purgatory) plus the Jack/Miranda confrontation Shepard settled (jack_miranda_dispute: appeased both), and the Suicide Mission itself (Jack held the biotic barrier, all-survived outcome per suicide_mission canon). Pragia/Teltin and Grissom get at most a glancing bridging mention, never the anchor. Jack's framing of "holding a barrier is a focus problem, not a strength problem" and "Cerberus bought a weapon and Shepard made a person" are her own editorializing on the record, not new corpus facts.
Revision per Thomas: Shepard's own AU record is now a load-bearing second thread, not a token mention. Jack is pitching HIM back to himself — every section now carries at least one beat where she cites something true of Shepard specifically as the proof, not just her own Purgatory/barrier/Brimstone/Murtock record. Sourced from config/canon/choices.yaml's Shepard AU overrides (Normandy-born, no parents, gang and drug problem before Anderson pulled him into N7; Sole Survivor of Akuze, the whole squad dead but him; Vanguard, biotic charge into the guns; alignment "Paragon, except against oppressors"; first name Thomas) plus the ME2/ME3 record most relevant to a focus-and-resolve pitch: Cerberus rebuilding him from a corpse via the Lazarus Project (a direct mirror to Jack's own tank), Mordin's death at the Shroud finishing the genophage cure, and Thessia — the one fight where Kai Leng actually got the better of him and walked off with Vendetta, which Jack uses as the counter-example, not the insult. Kai Leng's death at Cronos Station, days earlier in the same push on Cerberus's headquarters, closes the speech as proof the focus she's asking for is already proven, not a new trick.
Second revision per Thomas, correcting two errors: (1) the outline had previously let the closing section cite the Illusive Man's suicide as settled proof Jack could point back to. That confrontation happens on the Citadel, concurrent with or immediately after the London conduit assault itself — part of the endgame this speech is walking Shepard out the door toward, not something resolved before it. It has been cut entirely; Kai Leng's death at Cronos Station (a distinct, already-resolved event from the assault on Cerberus's headquarters, which happened before this morning) carries that closing beat on its own. (2) the whole episode was misdated as the evening before, ending in the two of them going to sleep. It is corrected throughout to the morning of the assault itself: the fleet is already massed, the plan already briefed, nothing left to prepare — Jack is waking Shepard and getting him moving, not tucking him in. No section still ends on rest; every "tonight"/"tomorrow" reference has been changed to "today," "now," or "in the next hour," and "The Last Quiet Night" is renamed "The Last Quiet Hour" to hold the tattoo-and-sentiment beat inside a tense pre-launch hush instead of an evening of repose. The Crucible's final choice and Shepard's fate at the end of it remain deliberately left out: that hasn't happened yet either, and reaching for it would still be narrator omniscience, not something Jack could actually voice this morning.
This does not strain the form. `motivational`'s brief is explicit that "the narrator's own history is fuel for the exhortation, not the subject of it" — and Jack's whole method here is to make Shepard's history do exactly that work on Shepard himself: he's not telling her own story for its own sake, she's holding up his record as the evidence because a room full of only Jack's proof lets him nod along without it landing on him. Spine stays `mixed` — some sections anchor to Jack's own events/scenes, some to Shepard's, most to both at once, which is precisely what a speech that argues from the listener's own life looks like structurally. No change to form.

evidence.text:
Citadel Arena: Geth Challenge was a side mission in the Mass Effect 3: Citadel DLC, available after Citadel Docks: Retake the Normandy, once the Armax Arsenal Arena opened with the rest of Silversun Strip. It was typically the first arena challenge Shepard received. After one arena match, Dave Shanel, self-styled "Anti-President" of the Citadel University Engineering Club, emailed the Combat Sim Controls. He said Shepard's match had drawn a following at the club, that a member poll had chosen geth over Reapers or Cerberus because those felt too much like the news, and asked for a match against geth on the Blasteroid map. The club could not pay but offered to build Shepard a weapon mod, as some members worked in weapons research.

To complete the challenge, Shepard played a combat match in the Armax Arsenal Arena against geth on the Blasteroid map; because it was the first challenge received, not all match options were available until non-mission matches had been completed. The challenge was not mutually exclusive with other arena challenges, such as the Medi-Gel Challenge. After a successful match, Shanel sent a follow-up email, and reading it awarded the SMG Power Magnifier weapon mod and +2 Reputation, with a joking suggestion that Shepard test the mod before trusting it.

Citadel Arena: Spin Zone Elite Challenge was a side mission in the Mass Effect 3: Citadel DLC, available after Citadel Docks: Retake the Normandy, once the Armax Arsenal Arena opened with the rest of Silversun Strip. After one arena match, Daksa Teller, Earth-Clan Talent Liaison for Elkoss Combine's Citadel Sports Division, emailed the Combat Sim Controls offering corporate sponsorship. Teller congratulated Shepard on recent arena victories, noted Shepard had not yet settled on a corporate sponsor, and offered a one-time cash stipend for top gear, asking Shepard to make an Elkoss "debut" by selecting the Spin Zone layout against Elite enemies and winning.

To complete the challenge, Shepard selected "Spin Zone" as the map and "Elite" enemies at the Combat Simulator Control terminal; Spin Zone was a bronze-level prize and Elite enemies a silver-level prize, both purchased with prior match winnings. Other settings were free, allowing other non-conflicting arena challenges such as the Thermal Clip Challenge or Medi-Gel Challenge to be completed in the same match. Afterward Teller sent a second email praising Shepard as "the paradigm," promising to file the paperwork and arrange a future meeting. Receiving and reading the second email granted 5,000 credits and +2 Reputation.

evidence.text:
The Armax Arsenal Arena was a combat simulator complex on the Citadel's Silversun Strip, introduced in the Mass Effect 3: Citadel DLC. It featured a large rectangular room capable of projecting fully immersive holographic environments and scenarios for public entertainment. Spectators watched from upper areas outside the room and bought refreshments at a nearby food kiosk. Combat participants redeemed prizes at a company store, used procurement and weapon upgrade terminals, and could be treated in an adjacent infirmary. Kiosks were staffed by VIs in the form of female turians. Below the spectators' level was an athletes-only area with a scenario-setting terminal and a ready room containing an armor selection computer, a weapon bench, a rules datapad, and the elevator to the simulator. The venue started nearly empty and grew more crowded with spectators as more matches were fought.

Commander Shepard battled holographic enemies to score points and earn prizes, receiving a complimentary pass from the arena staff after retaking the Normandy. Initially only Cerberus and geth enemy sets were available at the Foot Soldier level; additional maps, enemy factions (Reapers, Collectors, and Mirror Match), ally licenses, and score modifiers were unlocked as prizes. Enemies could be fought at Foot Soldier, Elite, and Super Elite challenge levels. Up to two squad members could provide support, including former squadmates Urdnot Wrex, Miranda Lawson, Jack, Jacob Taylor, Samara, Grunt, Zaeed Massani, and Kasumi Goto, provided they were alive and their loyalty issues resolved and their ally licenses purchased from the Bronze prize pool. Maps included Wingman, Blasteroid, Spin Zone, Prime Evil, The Armax Classic, Pain Train, Brimstone, and Fatal Error. Six score modifiers, such as No Medi-Gel and One-Shot Player Shields, adjusted scoring bonuses.

evidence.text:
Citadel Arena: Charity Reaper Challenge was a side mission in the Mass Effect 3: Citadel DLC, available after Citadel Docks: Retake the Normandy, once the Armax Arsenal Arena opened with the rest of Silversun Strip. After Shepard completed some arena matches, an asari named Manava T'Khanna emailed the Combat Sim Controls. She wrote as a parent rather than a fundraiser: her daughter Lati had been diagnosed with a cerebral tumor a year earlier, had the bad tissue removed by microsurgery machines, and faced a slow recovery with only partial use of her limbs. Lati had wanted to be a huntress and wished to see Commander Shepard compete live; a small charity called Help a Dream had brought her to the Citadel. Manava asked Shepard to fight the toughest Reapers in the simulator and dedicate the match to Help a Dream.

To complete the challenge, Shepard set the simulator to Reapers at Super Elite difficulty, both of which had to be purchased with prior winnings as the silver-level Reaper Combat Set and the gold-level Super Elite enemy set, and completed the match. Any squadmates and modifiers were allowed, so other arena challenges such as the Prothean Challenge or Medi-Gel Challenge could be finished simultaneously. Afterward Manava sent a grateful second email, calling Shepard a hero rather than just a soldier. Receiving and reading it granted +15 Reputation.

evidence.text: - According to The Art of the Mass Effect Universe, the Atlas was first intended to be a heavy version of the YMIR Mech with a soldier inside. Eventually, a canopy was added to protect the soldier, and the Atlas was made even larger than the YMIR Mech. - An avatar prop of the Atlas is available on the Xbox Marketplace (called the "Cerberus Atlas" in the Avatar Store). It costs USD $2\.99 and is one of the few props that is larger than the avatar itself. - An aquatic variation of the Atlas mech, known as the Triton ADS, appears in the Mass Effect 3: Leviathan DLC pack. - An image of a destroyed Atlas unit marked with the emblem of the Talons can be seen in the Talons' communication feed. - During Mass Effect 3: Citadel, the CAT6 mercenaries deploy a single Atlas of their own against Shepard. This Atlas is functionally identical to normal Cerberus Atlas units, but sports a CAT6 gray camouflage pattern. - In Greek mythology, Atlas was the name of a Titan who was forced by Zeus to hold the sky up because he and his brother sided against Zeus in the Titanomachy. - The Atlas follows the theme of naming mechanical enemies after human mythological figures (A la the FENRIS, YMIR and LOKI mechs), but borrows its namesake from Greek mythology instead of Norse.

evidence.text: - The Atlas is slow and makes for a large target, but should not be underestimated. When attacking the Atlas from the front, take cover immediately and watch for when it moves its rocket launcher arm to fire. At melee range the Atlas can easily grab the player for an instant kill, though can only perform the grab after executing a regular melee attack first. Sustained weapons fire and powers should eventually destroy an Atlas provided the player can attack from a safe distance and in cover. - In single\-player, an Atlas fires its mass accelerator cannon in four shots per burst. In multiplayer, the Atlas fires a three shot volley. It is best to remain in cover until the shots have been fired, though the Atlas will usually fire its guided missile after firing a cannon volley. - While the Atlas very visibly telegraphs its rocket, charge and ground slam attack, no such warning is given for the shots from its powerful accelerator cannon, which can quickly and with no warning whatsoever inflict heavy damage on an unsuspecting player. - The Atlas can only use its instant kill Grab attack shortly after performing a ground slam or sweeping melee. Consequently, while an Atlas is recovering from its slam may seem like an opening to close in for a melee attack, it is the *worst* time to do so. - An Atlas that has taken damage to its armor discharges white electrical sparks, which can be seen even through smoke screens. - The Atlas's tactical value is twofold: initially, it draws fire and protects the deployment of softer targets nearby, protecting them until they can take cover or advance on players' positions. Second, because of its extreme damage output and the amount of ordnance it can soak, the Atlas acts as a pressure unit, slowly but surely taking over defended areas by forcing you to retreat. For both of these reasons, it is important to take an Atlas out quickly. - **Hijacking:** In single\-player, once an Atlas's shields have been taken down, the cockpit window can be shattered. This requires a considerable amount of sustained fire, but breaking the window will leave the pilot vulnerable to attack. Killing the pilot (who has no more health than an Assault Trooper) may allow the Atlas to be hijacked, potentially awarding an Achievement. This is not possible in multiplayer. - Killing the pilot of an Atlas is not an efficient way of taking one down—it requires a great amount of damage dealt to the canopy (roughly half of the Atlas' full Armor), preferably with a sniper rifle. This tactic also requires that the Atlas not be targeted anywhere other than the canopy, and that normally very effective powers such as Incinerate, Carnage and Proximity Mine not be used. If attempting to hijack an Atlas in single\-player, it may be a good idea to manually order your squadmates to attack other targets. This task becomes significantly easier using an armor piercing sniper rifle such as the Widow or Javelin. A headshot against the pilot through the intact canopy can open the atlas with little effort. - If Shepard manages to hijack an Atlas, it is best to keep the enemy Combat Engineers alive, since they will on occasions repair the controlled Atlas. This is very useful when facing hordes of tougher enemies. - If an Atlas is left empty, Cerberus troops may try taking control of it. - An empty atlas mech can be found intact in Grissom Academy: Emergency Evacuation, next to a combat engineer and multiple of them during Priority: Cerberus Headquarters in the back of the hangar. - The Atlas can be successfully attacked with Sabotage and turned against other nearby enemies. However, Atlases build up immunity to the power over time, and the same Atlas will not stay hacked as long with each subsequent use of Sabotage (eventually becoming immune). - In multiplayer, the Cobra Missile Launcher will instantly kill an Atlas and if well placed, can take out multiple Atlas mechs at once. However, on Platinum, an Atlas will sometimes survive a rocket but with no shields and very little armour left (mostly seems to happen at long range). - Repeated use of Warp followed by Throw will create Biotic Explosions heavily damaging the Atlas and any enemies nearby as well. This is true even when the Warp and Throw abilities may appear "orange" on the power wheel, and is especially effective because the Throw ability has a fast recharge. Upgrading the combo damage and recharge rates on these abilities makes this tactic even more effective. - Debuffs that reduce armor or increase the damage a target takes like Expose\-evolved Warp, Cryo Blast, and Proximity Mine with the Damage Taken evolution are extremely effective against Atlases.

evidence.text:
The Atlas was a large piloted Cerberus mech encountered in Mass Effect 3 and also fielded by the CAT6 mercenaries in Mass Effect 3: Citadel. Cerberus's research arm built it by combining the armor and firepower of a YMIR mech with the tactical judgment of a trained human pilot seated inside. An element zero core allowed it to be air-dropped onto a battlefield with minimal impact damage. Its thick armor included a transparent canopy of a proprietary polycrystalline composite that Alliance engineers hypothesized was a synthetic sapphire with crack- and heat-resistant interlayers. Though unwieldy in the field, its antipersonnel machine guns and heavy durability made it a serious threat, and unprepared encounters were expected to cause heavy casualties.

Offensively the Atlas carried a rocket launcher that dealt area damage plus burn-over-time, and a high-powered mass accelerator cannon fired in bursts (four shots in single-player, three in multiplayer). It launched guided missiles that were very hard to evade, and at close range it could swing or slam its claw arm or grab and crush a target for an instant kill, though only after a normal melee attack first. Destroyed Atlas mechs exploded violently, dealing severe damage through cover and terrain even after death. Defensively it had durable shields and armor, destructible armor plating on the shoulders, knees, and crotch, smoke grenades, and weak points at the canopy and rear exhaust port. It took 24% less damage from all Power Combos.

Recommended tactics included staying in cover, using armor-debuffing powers such as Expose-evolved Warp, Cryo Blast, and Proximity Mine, repeated Warp-Throw biotic explosions, Sabotage (to which Atlases built immunity over time), and the Cobra Missile Launcher in multiplayer for instant kills. In single-player, once its shields were down, sustained fire could shatter the canopy and leave the pilot, who had no more health than an Assault Trooper, vulnerable; killing the pilot could let Shepard hijack the Atlas and potentially earn an Achievement. Empty Atlas units could be found intact during Grissom Academy: Emergency Evacuation and Priority: Cerberus Headquarters. Per The Art of the Mass Effect Universe, it was first conceived as a heavier YMIR variant with a soldier inside before a protective canopy was added and the frame enlarged. An aquatic variant, the Triton ADS, appeared in Mass Effect 3: Leviathan.

evidence.text:
Grissom Academy: Emergency Evacuation was a Mass Effect 3 mission acquired after Priority: Palaven, when Samantha Traynor and EDI determined that a turian rescue signal answering an Academy evac request was actually a Cerberus fake and the station was still in danger. Cerberus forces were attacking Grissom Academy in the Petra Nebula to kidnap its students, most of whom were producing Alliance tech or training as military biotics. The mission had to be completed before Priority: The Citadel II or it was permanently failed.

With too many Cerberus ships to fight, Joker created a diversion so Shepard's shuttle could enter a cargo hold opened by Kahlee Sanders, who went back with Anderson to his Spectre-candidate days. Shepard freed Sanders from the security office, then fought through corridors and rooms rescuing scattered students, including Reiley Bellarmine and his dying sister Seanne. In Orion Hall, biotic students held off Assault Troopers and an Atlas; if a Mass Effect 2 save was imported and Jack survived the Suicide Mission, Jack led them and punched Shepard in the face on arrival (followed by a kiss if they had romanced). Otherwise Ensign Jason Prangley took charge. The squad then fought heavy waves of Centurions, Guardians, Combat Engineers, and Atlas mechs through two halves of the Atrium and a docking area, aided by empty Atlas mechs and by tech students including Octavia, with David Archer vouching for Shepard if Overlord was completed on the Paragon route.

During the final escape the wounded Rodriguez fell behind; whoever led the biotics smashed the glass to save her. If Jack led, everyone survived; if Prangley led, he was shot and killed. Afterward Shepard chose to assign the students as support (rolled into the Alliance 103rd Marine Division, +50 war assets, Paragon) or as a frontline Biotic Company (+75 war assets, Renegade), a choice that also set Jack's epilogue slide. Rewards included 25,000 credits, weapon mods, the Mnemonic Visor, and the Serrice Council Chestplate. If the mission expired, Jack was captured, turned into a Phantom, and had to be killed at Cerberus Headquarters, and Gavin Archer could commit suicide during Arrae: Ex-Cerberus Scientists.

evidence.text:
Ensign Jason Prangley was a biotic student at Jon Grissom Academy. He arrived at Grissom at age six, a shy child who barely spoke, and was known for constantly reading and studying battles, with some peers calling him a brownnoser. He proved capable of leadership when circumstances demanded it.

During the 2186 Reaper invasion, Cerberus attacked Grissom Academy to forcibly conscript its gifted students. If Jack survived the Suicide Mission, Prangley was among the students she protected; he was nearly killed by Atlas fire before his teacher intervened. When Commander Shepard arrived, Jason aided the firefight, providing biotic support strikes so that he and his teacher could retreat to higher ground. Afterward Jack derided his biotic fields as "weak," and he noticeably improved in later battles.

If Jack did not survive the Suicide Mission, Prangley interacted with Shepard in her place during the evacuation. Shepard found him stepping up to save Ensign Rodriguez from Atlas fire. Jason reported that their commanding officer had been killed, leaving him assuming command, and spoke on the students' behalf that they needed time to recharge after the strenuous exertion of biotics. In this scenario, Prangley later died protecting Rodriguez again from Cerberus troops just short of the hijacked escape shuttles. The survivors eulogized him aboard the shuttles, and Shepard invoked his memory to motivate the other students, either channeling their anger at his loss or holding up his sacrifice as an example to follow. Datapads left by Cerberus troops around the Academy indicate Prangley was specifically targeted as a prized acquisition.

evidence.page: Jack (Subject Zero) — Character Analysis (Part 2) — Psyche and Arc
evidence.text:
Part 2 of a YouTube character analysis of Jack, focused on the psychology behind her behavior and the arc that leads her to the family she always wanted; much of it is the author's interpretation.

Jack arrives aboard the Normandy broken: psychologically tortured, conditioned to enjoy killing, then used and discarded by everyone she met after escaping her captors, so she lives on edge waiting for betrayal. She refuses to move on from her past. Her tattoos mark prisons, memorable kills, personal reasons, and some "just because"; her haircut is from the cult she ran with. She wears little clothing deliberately, believing nearly everyone wants to use her for sex, and uses it to read intentions. Kelly Chambers notes she pushes people away yet approaches sex casually and warns Shepard to "think twice" if he wants her respect. Given her childhood, Jack is entirely desensitized to death and crime; Cerberus built a Pavlovian link between narcotic euphoria and killing, so she feels bliss where others feel regret, kills without hesitation ("Every time someone dies and it's not me, my chances of survival go up"), and would kill a hostage as the simpler option. Her "no regrets" stance borders on narcissism and a refusal of accountability; asked whether she would do anything differently, she answers a flat "No."

The real wound is that she wants a family and acceptance but pushes everyone away first. The one exception was Murtock, a man she loved and ran jobs with. After robbing a heavily guarded weapons frigate they were separated; Murtock came back for her rather than take the score, Jack escaped in a shuttle, and he was left behind. Days later the shuttle played his pre-recorded message about the future they were meant to have and how much he loved her. Jack outwardly denies fault but shows survivor's-guilt signs. Her view of relationships: "You let someone get that close, it just means they need a shorter knife."

If Shepard shows genuine, non-sexual interest, her shell cracks; sleeping with her early instead breaks trust. Wanting to move on, Jack decides to blow up Teltin. There she meets Aresh, a dark reflection also stuck in the past, who wants to restart the facility to give the suffering meaning. Shepard can argue Jack out of killing him; letting Aresh live and destroying the facility gives her a revelation about what she could have become. With continued emotional support a relationship forms; in place of a sex scene they only kiss and lie in bed together. After the Collector Base and Shepard's surrender to the Alliance, Jack is alone again until the Alliance offers her a teaching post at Grissom Academy training biotic children ("Teltin if it were run by good people"). She wears more clothing, grows out her hair, and argues for her students to serve in a defensive, protective role rather than as biotic artillery. Reunited with Shepard, she says his attitude rubbed off on her and that her students and Shepard are the closest thing to family she has had. On shore leave, doubt briefly reverts her to her old self before Shepard again refuses to leave her. To show her love she gives Shepard a smaller version of her back tattoo on his right shoulder blade, so she can identify him "lying under a pile of rubble at the ass end of this war." Asked if she ever tattooed anyone else: "Nobody else mattered enough." Jack ends the trilogy with a family and, crucially, having made the effort to change.

evidence.text:
The Blue Suns were a "private security organization" that was in reality a ruthless, discreet, and expensive mercenary outfit operating in the Skyllian Verge. Members bore a blue sun tattoo, removed with acid wash during high-risk jobs. The group was mostly batarian, turian, and human, and used YMIR, FENRIS, and LOKI mechs. It was founded in 2160 by Zaeed Massani and Vido Santiago as a protection racket, Zaeed leading the men and Vido handling administration. A dispute over hiring batarians led to a 2165 power struggle in which Vido seized control and nearly killed Zaeed. Vido then hired batarians freely and installed Solem Dal'Serah as the public head of operations while remaining hidden as "Co-Executive Officer."

In Mass Effect: Revelation (2165), the Suns were hired by Edan Had'dah for the Sidon raid; Saren Arterius killed several, including Groto Ib-ba, during his investigation, and Suns under Skarr captured Kahlee Sanders before dying when an element zero refinery was destroyed. In Incursion (2183) a Suns–Collector exchange of humans on Omega was wiped out by Aria T'Loak. In Redemption the Suns recovered Commander Shepard's body from Alchera for the Shadow Broker but were ambushed by Liara T'Soni and Feron. In Foundation the Illusive Man hired Suns as a containment crew during Subject Zero's rampage.

In Mass Effect 2 (2185) Shepard repeatedly clashed with the Suns: they controlled Omega's Gozu District until the plague weakened their non-human members; they besieged Archangel (Garrus Vakarian) alongside Eclipse and Blood Pack under coordinator Tarak, aided by Sidonis's betrayal, and were destroyed with Tarak's gunship. The Suns ran the Purgatory prison under Warden Kuril, who betrayed Shepard during Jack's recruitment and was killed. Suns officer Jedore funded Okeer's krogan project on Korlus and killed him. On Zorya, Zaeed pursued Vido Santiago through a Blue Suns-controlled refinery. Other operations included Harkin's Citadel racket, Prothean dig-site raids on Joab and Kopis, and pirate raids via the MSV Strontium Mule and Sanctum base. evidence.text:
Ben Hislop was a human mercenary and munitions master who appeared in Mass Effect: Evolution. He signed up to fight turians after his brother was killed during the turian bombardment of Shanxi's settlements during the First Contact War, and fought in the resistance on occupied Shanxi. Recruited into Jack Harper's prohumanity movement, he formed a mercenary trio with Jack and Eva Coré, conducting guerrilla warfare under the employ of General Williams, and served as Jack's right-hand man.

On Shanxi, Ben's unit ambushed a turian patrol and he personally fought and captured the turian general Desolas Arterius with Jack's help. He wanted to execute Desolas but Jack kept the general alive for interrogation. On a mission to find the artifact Desolas sought, Ben antagonized him while Jack's scheme defeated the turian subordinates. Reaching the artifact inside a cave, Ben and Jack were ambushed by hooded figures revealed to be cyberized turians, which proved freakishly strong. When Ben touched the artifact to try to shut it off, he was electrocuted; Jack pried him free but was also affected, leaving both incapacitated. Desolas seized them and ordered Ben's body taken for study.

When Harper and Eva pursued Desolas to Illium, they found Ben alive but mutated into a synthetic form like the "meta-turians." He retained some sense of his identity but followed orders from Desolas and Saren, bringing the artifact, the Arca Monolith, to Palaven, where Desolas tried to replicate Harper's enhancement without creating mindless husks. The artifact commanded Ben to excavate a second artifact to accelerate the transformation. When Eva tried to haul Ben out and then to destroy the artifact, it commanded Ben to slam her head against a wall, killing her. Coming to his senses, a horrified Ben charged Desolas and rammed him into the artifact before he could shoot Harper; Saren tore Desolas away. Prolonged contact with the released energy instantly killed Ben, and his body was later vaporized when Saren ordered an orbital bombardment of the temple. Harper later included Ben's and Eva's names in his manifesto as he became the Illusive Man.

evidence.text: The **Skyllian Verge** is a largely undeveloped patch of space situated along the borders of Systems Alliance and batarian space. It is seen as a somewhat lawless area, with pirates and slavers both being known to operate freely, and a large number of "private security organizations" (mercenary groups), as well as freelancers, operate in the area. The area is known to be patrolled by the Systems Alliance military. However they do not have enough ships to adequately police the area, so in many instances by the time they arrive at a colony in trouble it is already too late. The batarians believed the Verge to be rightfully theirs and opposed the Alliance being allowed to colonize planets in the Verge. These tensions later led to the Skyllian Blitz.

evidence.text: Biotic abilities are of varying rarity and status in other species: - **Asari** \- All asari are naturally biotic to some degree, though not all choose to develop their abilities. Those who do pursue training usually display formidable ability. They do not require implants to use biotics effectively, nor do they need to undergo special training to acquire conscious neural control; their reproductive physiology grants them this ability from birth. Biotic ability is mandatory for asari who want to go into military service. The most powerful train as asari commandos. - **Batarians** \- There are some known batarian biotics who are trained as shock troopers and sentinels. - **Collectors** \- All Collectors have a latent biotic potential, which is activated if the Collector General takes control of their body and mind, transforming them into powerful and dangerous opponents. - **Drell** \- The drell assassin Thane Krios is a biotic. Many other drell join the war effort against the Reapers, acting as adepts and vanguards. - **Krogan** \- Krogan biotics are few in number, but all are extremely powerful and often train to become Krogan Battlemasters like Skarr or Wrex. Before the genophage, biotic krogan who enlisted in the military would rise quickly through the ranks; the other soldiers were in fear and awe of them, so their superiors recognized they would command great respect as officers and promoted them. The krogan developed a surgical procedure that was able to confer biotic ability, but the operation had a high mortality rate, so it was discontinued following the release of the genophage. - **Protheans** \- Javik is a Prothean biotic. He may casually mention they used to clean their teeth with biotics. Besides this, it is unknown how widespread Prothean biotics were before their extinction. - **Quarians** \- According to Tali, quarian biotics are very rare. It is speculated that this is due to their life aboard the Migrant Fleet. Element zero is such a rare resource that it is probably too precious to be "spent" on encouraging biotic potential in quarians, and because the quarians live aboard ships, any engine accident severe enough to release dust\-form element zero would also be fatal to the crew, and any expectant mother would only be exposed to the dust if they had a compromised environmental suit. - **Rachni** \- Rachni Brood Warriors appear to have some biotic abilities. - **Salarians** \- Salarian biotics are unusual and highly prized. The salarian military does not risk them in the front lines but instead uses them in intelligence services. - **Turians** \- Turian biotics are also uncommon, and generally not much more powerful than a human L3\. They are viewed with suspicion by the general turian infantry and tend to be relegated to special units called Cabals, which are employed for key missions. - **Volus** \- Some volus are trained as Adepts, Vanguards and Sentinels, although the Sentinels do not use biotic abilities. - **Vorcha** \- Some vorcha are trained as Sentinels. - To date, there has been no mention of the biotic abilities of the hanar, elcor, raloi, Leviathans, or yahg or what role (if any) biotics play in their respective societies.

evidence.text: Biotics possess extraordinary abilities, but they must live with minor inconveniences. The most obvious issue is getting adequate nutrition. Creating biotic mass effects takes such a toll on metabolism that active biotics develop ravenous appetites. The standard Alliance combat ration for a soldier is 3000 calories per day; biotics are given 4500, as well as a canteen of potent energy drink for quick refreshment after hard combat. Another issue is electric charge. Electricity accumulated in starship drive cores must be discharged, and so must the electricity in a biotic user. Biotics are prone to small static discharges when they touch metal. Unfortunately, human biotics also face suspicion and persecution, beginning with the popular misconception that they can read and control minds. Biotics symbolize the dehumanization of mankind to people philosophically or religiously opposed to gene modification and cybernetics. Militaries are the only organizations that always welcome biotics, offering them huge recruitment incentives.

They focus on combat potential, using biotics to disable and soften up their enemies while shielding themselves from return damage long enough to dispatch foes in a hail of gunfire. The Vanguard wears light armor to start with, though they can upgrade to medium armor, and they may gain specialist training in shotguns and pistols. They can also equip advanced bio\-amps to increase the strength of their biotics. All Krogan Battlemasters including Wrex belong to this class. The Vanguard class talent increases damage with shotguns and pistols, and increases biotic protection.

evidence.text:
Biotics was the ability of some lifeforms to create mass effect fields using element zero nodules embedded in body tissues, accessed and augmented through bio-amps. Biotic individuals could knock enemies over at range, lift them into the air, generate gravitational vortices to tear apart obstacles or enemies, or create protective barriers. Abilities fell into three categories: telekinesis (mass-lowering fields), kinetic fields (mass-raising fields), and spatial distortion (shifting fields that rip apart objects). Powers were triggered by "physical mnemonics," physical gestures that fired neurons in sequence.

All asari were naturally biotic from birth and required no implants or special training. Biotics of other species were individuals exposed to dust-form element zero in utero who developed eezo nodules throughout their nervous systems. Exposure rarely produced biotics; most exposed fetuses were unaffected, and others developed brain tumors or other complications. In humans, only about one in ten eezo-exposed infants developed usable talent, and in rare cases talents emerged in young adulthood through additional exposure. Identified biotics were typically fitted with a surgically implanted amplifier around puberty and then underwent long biofeedback training.

The first human biotics were born after starship accidents in the 2150s dispersed element zero over populated areas; the first known was female, dubbed "Subject White." Conatix Industries was founded to track exposed individuals and develop implants, and in 2160 established the BAaT programme on Jump Zero, which was shut down after the turian instructor Commander Vyrnnus was killed by a student. Human biotics were classed by implant model: L1, the notorious L2 (introduced 2167, powerful but often unstable and medically damaging), L3 (2170, stable but weaker), retrofit and experimental variants, L4 used in the Ascension Project, and L5x and L5n for Adepts and Vanguards by 2185. Dr. Ellen Ryder created the first human biotic implants. Human biotics faced widespread prejudice, while the Alliance military eagerly recruited them, granting them a 4,500-kilocalorie daily ration.

Among aliens, biotics varied in rarity: common and powerful in asari, rare and prized in salarians, uncommon and distrusted in turians (relegated to Cabals), few but extremely powerful in krogan (Battlemasters such as Skarr and Wrex), and very rare in quarians. Batarians, drell (Thane Krios), Collectors, Protheans (Javik), volus, and vorcha also produced biotics. Non-sapient biotic creatures existed on eezo-rich worlds like Thessia and Eingana, including Jack's biotic varren Eezo. Biotics were exceedingly rare or absent in the Andromeda galaxy.

evidence.text:
Cerberus Commandos were highly trained shock troopers used by Cerberus to perform operations and defend locations in the first Mass Effect. They formed a key part of the defense of Cerberus installations on Binthu and Nepheron, facilities conducting research on organisms such as Rachni Workers, Rachni Soldiers and Thorian Creepers.

Commandos were armed with assault rifles and shotguns and were deadly at close range. Rather than hold cover, they frequently charged to get around their enemy's cover and made sweeping, flanking attacks. They had relatively high health as well as shields, though powerful attacks and well-used cover were usually enough to weaken and neutralize them. Because they were fairly accurate and came in groups, crowd-control talents were useful against them; alternatively, on Binthu, releasing the captive test subjects could turn the fight into a three-way battle that drew fire away from the player.

evidence.text:
Hendel Mitra was a former Alliance soldier serving as Security Chief of the Ascension Project. Tall and muscular with rusty-brown hair and light brown skin, he was of part Scandinavian and part Indian ancestry, born in the suburbs of the New Calcutta megapolis on Earth. His mother's exposure to dust-form element zero during pregnancy gave him biotic powers rather than birth defects. Detected as a biotic, he was sent to BAaT for training, where the harsh military program's efforts to separate children from their families succeeded too well: he became permanently estranged from his family, refusing contact even after BAaT closed, and later enlisted in the Alliance military. Kahlee Sanders believed his BAaT experiences drove his determination to help Gillian Grayson. He is hinted to be homosexual through Kahlee's comments.

In Mass Effect: Ascension, Hendel was troubled by Paul Grayson's drug addiction and contact with Gillian, but was fiercely protective of all the Project's children. When Gillian unleashed a biotic storm in the cafeteria, he hesitated to stun her and used his own biotics to shield himself, afterward blaming himself and considering resignation. His protectiveness paid off when he caught Dr. Jiro Toshiwa administering cerebrospinal medication that triggered a seizure in Gillian; despite being stunned repeatedly, Hendel stayed conscious and kept her alive with CPR until EMTs arrived. After Jiro was exposed as a Cerberus operative, Hendel accompanied Kahlee, Gillian, and Paul Grayson to Omega, where they were captured by the Cerberus agent Pel, who planned to sell Hendel and Gillian to the Collectors. The quarian Lemm'Shal nar Tesleya broke them out, and they fled to the Migrant Fleet. During quarantine aboard the shuttle Hendel tutored Gillian in her biotics; he toured the Idenna with Kahlee and marveled at its free trading economy. When Cerberus sent Paul Grayson and the quarian Golo to extract Gillian, Hendel fought with his biotics and was badly hurt, but recovered enough to help defuse explosives aboard the Cyniad before it could destroy the Idenna. When Kahlee left with Paul as a captive, Hendel stayed aboard the Migrant Fleet as Gillian's protector for the Idenna's mission to find a new quarian homeworld.

In the first edition of Mass Effect: Deception (acknowledged by BioWare as containing lore discrepancies), Hendel and Gillian remained trusted crew of the Idenna. When the batarian slave ship Glory of Khar'shan boarded the vessel and the quarian security head Ugho was killed, Hendel took command and led the counterattack, and with Gillian's biotics the quarians seized the slaver ship. After the captured slave Hal McCann told Gillian her father was dead, Hendel left with her aboard the batarian ship to learn what had happened.

evidence.text:
Arvuna was a moon of the planet Dranen, located in the Aysur System of the Caleston Rift in the Milky Way. It became accessible in Mass Effect 3 after the mission Leviathan: Find Garneau. Classified as a water world because oceans or ice covered 90% of its surface, Arvuna hosted prodigious sea life as well as venomous arthropodal pests in its tropical zone whose metallic carapaces, similar to those found on Palaven, resisted radiation from Dranen's magnetosphere. Several well-shielded human colonies existed on Arvuna, though they were alienated from the Citadel Council and politically insignificant to the Traverse and Terminus Systems.

During the Reaper War the Reapers had not reached Arvuna, concentrating instead on the Balor system, which cut Arvuna off from the cluster's mass relay but served as evidence that the Reapers could not be everywhere at once. The Mass Effect 3 multiplayer map Firebase Hydra was located on Arvuna. Cerberus Daily News stories referenced the moon, including one about fishermen and marine biologists capturing a Deinorostrum there. Arvuna was originally slated for Mass Effect 2 and appears in that game's guide and files, but was cut before release; its earlier description differed significantly, mentioning avian species and human settlements totaling over a third of a billion inhabitants.

evidence.text: Engineer Donnelly works in the engine room with his best friend Gabriella Daniels. They graduated from the same class at a tech academy and served aboard the SSV Perugia at the Battle of the Citadel. After the battle, when the Alliance discredited the existence of the Reapers, Kenneth openly voiced his defense for Commander Shepard, bordering on insubordination, though he wasn't court\-martialled because of his engineering talents. This got him noticed by the Illusive Man. Gabby insisted to Kenneth that she be included in the Cerberus contract as she felt he would fall apart without her. If Shepard asks about why Kenneth joined Cerberus, he replies that he joined to "kick the Collectors right in the daddy\-bags." If asked, Kenneth and Gabriella tell Shepard about their maintenance problems with the FBA arrays. Kenneth begins on a detailed technical description of the problem, till Gabby cuts him short and explains to the Commander that they need FBA couplings. If Shepard purchases the couplings from Nashan Stellar Dynamics, Kenneth invites them to a game of Skyllian\-five poker. The Commander can choose to join in, simply decline the invite or downright forbid gambling. Kenneth frequently chats with Gabby about new ship upgrades and the crew. He also makes a lot of comments about other women aboard the Normandy, which leads to teasing and scolding from Gabby. Kenneth makes remarks about the snugness of Tali'Zorah vas Neema's suit "in all the right places", about Jack's simultaneous sexiness and viciousness, and about Miranda's uniform making him stand "at attention." Kenneth is among the Normandy crew members abducted by the Collectors when they invade the Normandy, and he will die if Shepard and the squad take too long to rescue the crew. |  | ***“There won't be an Earth left to save...”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 3** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

evidence.text:
Gabriella "Gabby" Daniels was a former Alliance engineer, a Cerberus operative in the Lazarus Cell, and an engineer aboard the Normandy SR-2 in 2185. More serious and formal than her fellow engineer and best friend Kenneth Donnelly, she preferred to get straight to the point. The two graduated from the same tech academy class and served aboard the SSV Perugia at the Battle of the Citadel. Afterward, when Kenneth publicly defended Commander Shepard against the Alliance's denial of the Reapers, Cerberus recruited him; Gabby insisted on being included in the contract, believing he would fall apart without her.

Gabby loved starship engines and worked the engineering deck beside Kenneth, often chatting about ship upgrades and crew, scolding Kenneth for perverted comments, and teasing him about Jack before warning him she was a psychopathic murderer. She was among the Normandy crew abducted by the Collectors and would die if Shepard took too long to rescue the crew during the suicide mission.

If she survived, Gabby was taken into custody when the Alliance impounded the Normandy in 2186; Shepard could use Spectre status to free her back to the engine room. She and Kenneth were both approached again by Cerberus during the Normandy's downtime but refused on Gabby's intuition. Back at work on the Alliance Normandy SR-2, they resumed their old banter. Chief Engineer Adams praised Gabby as knowing propulsion theory better than most physicists and thanked Shepard for recruiting her. If both survived and Shepard sided with Gabby in their argument, she and Kenneth could begin a romance and later be caught embracing in the sub-deck. After the war, if Shepard used the Crucible with sufficient preparation, Kenneth, Gabby, and Major Coats oversaw reconstruction efforts in a devastated London. A programming error tied the Gabby and Ken banter to Shepard being good friends with Ashley, fixed by the Extended Cut. In an unmodified, non-imported Mass Effect 3, Gabby's name appeared on the Normandy's memorial wall.

evidence.page: The SSV Normandy SR-2 (Part 1) — Origin and EDI
evidence.text: The SR-2's most significant upgrade over the SR-1 is EDI — the Enhanced Defense Intelligence — an AI represented by a floating blue holographic sphere at terminals throughout the ship. EDI provides basic information about the Normandy and Cerberus, and functions as the ship's electronic-warfare defense. Because of the danger of a rogue AI, EDI was given behavioral blocks and could not interface with ship systems directly. When the Collectors boarded and abducted most of the crew, an emergency response — EDI working with Joker — released those blocks, granting EDI full control of the Normandy. Before Shepard's crew defected from Cerberus back to the Systems Alliance, EDI also served as the Illusive Man's eyes and ears aboard, monitoring the ship's many listening devices and sending him regular reports. During this time the Illusive Man restricted Shepard's access to some of EDI's files and capabilities — EDI surmised he did not want Shepard to know everything about Cerberus. EDI gained access to anti-Reaper algorithms and devoted significant processing power to analyzing them. Asked how she could hope to fight beings millions of years more advanced, she revealed that she was designed in part with technology from Sovereign's remains, and is therefore herself partly based on Reaper technology. evidence.text:
Despoina: Leviathan was the final mission of the Mass Effect 3: Leviathan DLC, available after Leviathan: Scan Locations once scanning 2181 Despoina revealed a faint trace of Leviathan's energy signature. The mission began when Shepard's team landed on the ocean planet. During descent, a mysterious pulse disabled the Normandy shuttle, and Steve Cortez set it down on one of the floating shipwrecks littering the ocean. Datapads among the wrecks told the story of the MSV Monarch's crew, who crash-landed after a similar pulse, ran short of rations, and were gradually enthralled by organic spherical artifacts, turning violent and refusing to leave.

A Sovereign-class Reaper descended and Reaper forces (Husks, Cannibals, Marauders, and Brutes) attacked repeatedly while Cortez repaired the shuttle, though the pulse kept striking and forced him to land again. With the shuttle unable to fly and the Normandy unable to safely approach, the team resolved to press on and find Leviathan. Cortez proposed using a Triton ADS mech stored in a sealed section of the wreck; Shepard carried the shuttle's power cells to sockets to charge the bay door open while fending off Reaper waves. Once inside, Shepard piloted the Triton, which handled like an Atlas, to clear out endlessly reinforcing Brutes and enemies.

Shepard then dove in the Triton to the ocean floor, losing contact with Cortez partway down due to interference. Near the probe Shepard had sent earlier, at a depth around 3,200 meters, Shepard encountered Leviathan. The entity explained its race's history and reasons for staying out of the war, and initially declared that Shepard must remain while the Reapers harvested everyone else, but was ultimately convinced to help for its own reasons. During the ascent, a Brute on the surface turned against other Reaper forces, and as Shepard escaped in the repaired shuttle, a ship-disabling pulse struck the pursuing Reaper, sending it crashing into the ocean. Shepard woke aboard the shuttle; if Ann Bryson had survived her ordeal relatively unharmed, she spoke with Shepard over the comm. Completion granted the Leviathan Enthrallment Team War Asset (and Ann Bryson as an asset if not incapacitated), and made Dominate available as a bonus power in the Med Bay.

evidence.text:
Shiagur was a krogan warlord and one of the few fertile krogan females remaining after the widespread deployment of the genophage, circa 700 CE. She used her fertility to amass male followers, who competed among themselves for the right to have children with her. Despite her legendary reputation, her band was not particularly powerful, and she was defeated and killed at Canrum by turian forces during the last stages of the Krogan Rebellions. Vengeful krogan admirers retaliated against her killers, ultimately causing thousands of casualties.

Shiagur's bloodline remained a status symbol among later krogan, with her direct descendants bearing clan brands proving their lineage; Nakmor Drack and his granddaughter Nakmor Kesh were among them, and the tank-bred Grunt carried some of her genetic legacy through Okeer's selection of "worthy" krogan. Being compared to Shiagur was considered a mark of honor: the Urdnot Shaman might bestow the compliment on a female Shepard who understood the krogan better than some of their own kind, and her name was invoked in a song Mordin Solus could sing for Eve.
